object.name: evi.clip~
object.digest: Anti-aliased clipping algorithms for your audio
object.description: A collection of four anti-aliased clipping algorithms: hard clip, soft clip, diode clip, asymmetric clip. Hard and soft are better anti-aliased and can take higher input gain before aliasing than the diode and asymmetric clippers. To be used whenever clamping of audio is required, <o>evi.clip~</o> should do a good job of protecting your precious audio.
object.discussion: This object is for all those MSP users who use [<o>clip~</o>  -1. 1.] or [<o>tanh~</o>] at the end of their audio chains. You should never do this - it destroys your audio and aliases like hell. Use <o>evi.clip~</o> instead. It can anti-alias very large gain inputs whilst retaining the clipping functionality you seek.

inlets.digest: Audio In that must be treated nicely

attributes.name: clip
attributes.description: Select the clipping function used. 0=hard (default), 1=soft, 2=diode, 3=asymmetric. 'Hard' is the equivalent of [clip~ -1. 1], 'soft' is the equivalent of [tanh~], 'diode' is a static model of a 12AX7, 'aymmetric' is a static version of Laurent de Soras' 'Gloubi Boulga'.

attributes.name: oversampling
attributes.description: Regardless of this setting, hard and soft clippers are 2nd order antiderivatives and thus already have excellent behaviour with @oversampling=0. Oversampling=1 is 2x oversampling, oversampling=2 is 4x oversampling.
